In the cubic structure of ZnS (Zinc blend) of edge length `$a$' :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Distance between two nearest $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ ions is $\dfrac a2$}
\opt{B}{Distance between two nearest $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ ions is $\dfrac a{\sqrt2}$}
\opt{C}{The angle made by the lines connecting any $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ to any two of its nearest neighbours is $60^\circ$}
\opt{D}{The angle made by the lines connecting any $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ to any two of its nearest neighbours is $109^\circ28'$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS01-P1-CHEM-S1-Q11, source={TMAS - Test 01 (09 Jul 2023)}, paper=1, qno=11, type=single, subtopic={Defects}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: non stoichiometric defect | steps: charge balance; ratio of Cu 2 plus and 1 plus}]

\opt{B}{1 : 12.5}
\opt{C}{1 : 23}
\opt{D}{1 : 24}
\end{qoptions}

\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS01-P1-CHEM-S2-Q05, source={TMAS - Test 01 (09 Jul 2023)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Unit cells}, answer={4}, answer_src=solved, working={Cell volume $(0.6\ \mathrm{nm})^3=2.16\times10^{-22}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, mass $\approx1.08\times10^{-22}$ g, i.e. $\approx4.07$ molecules; 4 per cell}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: unit cell density | steps: volume; mass; molecules per cell}]
Methane when solidified crystallizes in a structure having cubic unit cell with edge length of 0.6 nm. The density of solid $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is only slightly greater than the density of liquid $\mathrm{CH_4}$. If the density of liquid $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is 0.5 g/cm$^3$, the number of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ molecules per unit cell in solid crystal of methane is :
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS01-P1-CHEM-S2-Q07, source={TMAS - Test 01 (09 Jul 2023)}, paper=1, qno=7, type=numerical, subtopic={Unit cells}, answer={8}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S3 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: BCC crystal, ideal gas | steps: moles from the gas law; atoms; unit cells; cell volume; scale}]
A cube shaped crystal of an alkali metal, 2 mm on an edge, was vaporised in a 800 mL flask. The pressure of the resulting vapour was 7.6 mm at 727$^\circ$ C. The structure of the solid metal is known to be body centred cubic. If volume of each unit cell of this crystal is [$P\times10^{-27}$ m$^3$] then find value of (3P) ? [Given : $R=0.08$ L-atm mol$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, $N_A=6\times10^{23}$]
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS01-P2-CHEM-S1-Q03, source={TMAS - Test 01 (09 Jul 2023)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=multi, subtopic={Packing}, answer={B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: spinel structure | steps: holes in CCP; ions per cell; formula; reduce}]
Spinel is an important class of oxides consisting of two types of metal ions with the oxide ions arranged in CCP pattern. The normal spinel has one-eighth of the tetrahedral holes in the crystal structure occupied by one type of metal ions and one-half of the octahedral holes in the crystal structure occupied by another type of metal ions. One such type of a spinel is formed by $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ions. The simplest formula of this spinel can not be :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$}
\opt{B}{$\mathrm{Zn_2AlO_4}$}
\opt{C}{$\mathrm{Zn_2Al_3O_4}$}
\opt{D}{$\mathrm{ZnAlO_2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS01-P2-CHEM-S3-Q03, source={TMAS - Test 01 (09 Jul 2023)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=numerical, subtopic={Defects}, answer={2}, answer_src=key, difficulty=9, diff_parts={K2 S3 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: crystal defects, density | steps: mass of boron; atoms; density change; vacancies filled; percent}]
A strong current of trivalent gaseous boron passed through a silicon crystal decreases the density of the crystal due to part replacement of silicon by boron and due to interstitial vacancies created by missing Si atoms. In one such experiment, one gram of silicon is taken and the boron atoms are found to be 1000 ppm, by mass, when the density of the Si crystal decreases by 12\%. The percentage of missing vacancies due to silicon, which are filled up by boron atoms is (Atomic masses : Si = 30, B = 11)\\
\textbf{[Give your answer as nearest integer]}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS02-P1-CHEM-S1-Q01, source={TMAS - Test 02 (06 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=single, subtopic={Unit cells}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: density of a crystal | steps: cell volume; mass of six molecules; molar mass}]
A protein molecule crystallizes as orthorhombic with $a=80$ \AA, $b=30$ \AA{} and $c=125$ \AA. If there are six protein molecules per unit cell and density of unit cell is $1.5$ g/ml then the molar mass of protein in kg/mole is :\\
(Given : $N_A=6\times10^{23}$)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{45000}
\opt{B}{45}
\opt{C}{15}
\opt{D}{75}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS02-P2-CHEM-S1-Q01, source={TMAS - Test 02 (06 Aug 2023)}, paper=2, qno=1, type=multi, subtopic={Packing}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=solved, working={BCC cell edge 400 A, FCC edge 500 A (with $\sqrt6=2.5$); volume falls by $3\times10^{-9}$ m$^3$, work $=P\Delta V=0.3$ J; FCC is denser}, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S3 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: crystal structures, work | steps: edge lengths; volumes; change of volume; work; density}]
When $1000$ bar constant external pressure is applied on BCC crystal of metal `$M$' then its crystalline structure is changed from BCC to FCC. If radius of metal is $100\sqrt3$ \AA{} and initially in the BCC lattice there were $2\times10^{15}$ unit cells then : [Take $\sqrt6=2.5$]
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Work done on the metal crystal is $0.3$ J}
\opt{B}{Work done on the metal crystal is $0.7$ J}
\opt{C}{When crystal changes its structure from BCC to FCC its density increases.}
\opt{D}{When crystal changes its structure from FCC to BCC its density remains constant.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
